summary: Round 25 re-check (10:17-10:50Z 28 Sep). The new fact that decides the choice: probe 48 exp79a (exp70g + coordinject/CI, ALPHA 0.5, MAX_UM 3.0) = 0.957 with an attributable UP (33 teams). It is the first public '+' for a post-CSV, coordinate-only change, and it was measured on an embryo the refiner never saw. Three old conclusions rested on the premise that 'post-CSV coordinate changes do not move the LB' (float output tied twice). I re-checked all three and ran a new CPU lab: the kernel integer path on the 4 CI-lab clips, 12 arms, official metric, in-sample for the refiner. (A) 'No ALPHA/MAX_UM follow-up rung' (27 Sep 16:08Z (4)/(5), R18-RC-A; exp76b OUT) -> REVIVED. MAX_UM is a zero-code --set knob. It is the best lab arm: MAX_UM 2.0 gives +0.0045 over base vs +0.0022 for the scored MAX_UM 3.0, MAX_UM 4.0 gives +0.0002, ALPHA 0.65 +0.0011, ALPHA 0.35 -0.0015 and ALPHA 1.0 -0.0050. The CI knobs never had arms, because the 28 Sep knob inventory was built on exp70g, which has no CI. Proposal: exp89a = exp79a + COORDINJECT_MAX_UM 2.0, as the '? test' in the 29 Sep 00:05-01:45Z window. (B) Embryo-constant z shift of +0.1 voxel (R8-RC-A; sent to the post-deadline list only because of R8, 26 Sep 11:06Z) -> the mechanism survives CI but is not confirmed on it. The refiner is itself z-biased (+0.3..+0.6 um on 3/4 clips), so CI leaves a residual z bias of +0.44..+0.70 um. CI + z0.1 cuts the matched error again on 4/4 clips, yet its edge J is -0.0009 against CI (noise level; z -0.1 reads +0.0014). Keep it as a spare that needs new code. It is slotted only if a W4 slot would otherwise be empty. (C) 'CI is public-only; its private prior is unknown to slightly negative; there is no like-for-like transfer record' (27 Sep 16:08Z (2), 28 Sep 04:31Z card (1), R22-RC-A) -> OVERTURNED in part. Probe 48 is an out-of-embryo transfer record: +0.001 display with an UP. CI lowers the matched localisation error on 4/4 lab clips in both embryos (44b6 -0.05/-0.08 um, 6bba -0.28/-0.16 um). The mechanism is averaging two estimators, which is not embryo-specific. The CI caveat on the finals card should be rewritten. The answer to the user's pending question 'may morning files be CI files?' should be yes, with a 09:30Z cutoff. All lab numbers are in-sample for the refiner and come from a handful of edges on 2 clips (a sign-noise level). Public reads decide. Lab output: research/wf_ideas_v4/round25/ci_zshift_out.json.

findings.what: CI (coordinject) knob arms: COORDINJECT_MAX_UM and COORDINJECT_ALPHA. OLD VERDICT: pre-registered closed. (1) CONTEXT 27 Sep 16:08Z (4) 'Out: ... exp76b (MAX_UM knob rung)'. (2) (5) 'display tie -> no alpha/MAX_UM follow-up; attributable UP -> one 29 Sep stack ... with the same knobs (ALPHA 0.5, MAX_UM 3.0)'. (3) R18-RC-A: 'no alpha/MAX_UM follow-up rung (float output tied twice)'; 'no retune'. The evidence was the premise that post-CSV coordinate changes do not transfer (float output: lab +0.0018..+0.0025, LB ties in probes 32/33), plus an alpha-unstable 4-clip in-sample lab. WHAT CHANGED: (a) Probe 48 exp79a = 0.957 with an UP of 33 teams (CONTEXT 09:35Z), so the post-CSV premise is falsified on public for CI. (b) Aggressive mode, and the 743929 process the team adopted (two arms per knob, arms off the current best). The current best IS the CI file, and the 28 Sep knob inventory (knobarms_28sep, 93 knobs) was taken from exp70g, which has no CI, so the CI knobs never had arms. (c) Both knobs are zero-code --set keys (tools/coordinject_patch.py l.24-26: MAX_UM (0,7], ALPHA (0,1]). They leave topology, the refiner work and the runtime unchanged: the refiner runs the same videos, and only the snap/blend rule of the CSV rewrite changes. MEASURED NOW: kernel integer path (coordinject_positions + coordinject_cell) on rounded exp60 final nodes, 4 clips, official metric, pooled adj edge J vs base. MAX_UM 3 / ALPHA 0.5 (scored) +0.00215; MAX_UM 2.0 +0.00453 (per clip 0 / +0.0125 / 0 / +0.0079; 6bba_bb9f20c3 +5 TP / -5 FP over the scored arm; 44b6_c50204e0 recovers the TP that the scored arm loses); MAX_UM 4.0 +0.00020; ALPHA 0.65 +0.00111 (c502 -5 TP); ALPHA 0.35 -0.00146; ALPHA 1.0 -0.00498. These reproduce bigger_levers/check_coord_refiner.notes.md exactly. NEW VERDICT: REVIVED as the one CI knob arm. MAX_UM 2.0 is the only arm that beats the scored setting in the lab, and it does so on both clips that move. Its direction (a tighter snap, fewer far re-assignments) is also the lower-risk one: it moves a subset of the rows the scored file already moved. ALPHA arms stay out: 0.65 and 1.0 lose on c502, and 0.35 loses. MAX_UM 4.0 is the 'other direction' arm and is lab-flat. Caveats: in-sample for the refiner; the effect rests on ~10 edges on 2 clips; JT (743929) saw the lab sign wrong 4/4. Public odds that exp89a displays >= 0.958: ~0.2-0.3. P(<= 0.956): ~0.2.

findings.what: Embryo-constant z shift of +0.1 voxel (I-041/I-029; R8-RC-A). OLD VERDICT: R8-RC-A re-opened it (56-clip x138 lab +0.00161, 44b6 +0.00251, 6bba +0.00153, bootstrap P(<=0) 0.00). CONTEXT 26 Sep 11:06Z then sent it to the post-deadline list, because R8 allowed no new code and no retraining ('~+0.0003 expected out-of-sample'). The counter-anchors were Canh's forum xyz correction (-0.0031 on LB) and float output (coordinate-only, LB tie twice). WHAT CHANGED: (1) R8 is lifted and aggressive mode is on. (2) Probe 48 shows that a coordinate-only post-CSV change CAN move the public display, which removes the float-output anchor. (3) CI now sits in the base, so the question becomes whether CI already removes the z bias. MEASURED NOW (4 CI-lab clips, Hungarian 4 um, GT - pred): the refiner ALONE is z-biased positive (+0.61 / -0.03 / +0.30 / +0.60 um). The V1284 base is +0.69 / -0.17 / +0.75 / +0.39. After CI a0.5 it is +0.70 / -0.18 / +0.61 / +0.44, so CI barely touches z; its gain is mostly xy and variance (mean matched 3D error 1.836->1.782, 1.517->1.435, 1.548->1.264, 1.511->1.356). CI + z0.1 cuts the matched error again on 4/4 clips (1.748 / 1.415 / 1.219 / 1.325), but pooled edge J is +0.00130 against CI's +0.00215 (-0.0009; one clip, 2 TP). z0.2 gives +0.00130 and z -0.1 gives +0.00351, so the edge read is pure sign noise at n=4. Base + z0.1 on these 4 clips is -0.00022, against +0.0016 on the 56-clip lab. NEW VERDICT: the mechanism is ALIVE ON TOP OF CI: a positive residual z bias on 3/4 clips, both embryos, and consistent error cuts. It is NOT confirmed on edge J, because the 4-clip CI bed has no power for it. It still needs new code (a COORDINJECT_ZSHIFT_VOX knob applied to the blended float before coordinject_cell rounding, plus tests), and it would take a CI-latency slot (~9.3-9.5 h). Rank: below R25-RC-A. Not a finals lever, since its private sign depends on the hidden embryos' annotation convention (Canh -0.0031 anchor). The 56-clip non-CI lab is the only powered evidence.

findings.what: The CI finals caveat and private prior. OLD VERDICT: (1) CONTEXT 27 Sep 16:08Z (2): 'A coordinject file is PUBLIC-ONLY ... caveat post-CSV integer coordinate shift, ~1e-4 nudge read on one embryo, refiner lab in-sample'. (2) 28 Sep 04:31Z FINALS CARD (1): 'CI files info-only (post-CSV coordinate shift, in-sample 4-clip lab, no like-for-like LB record)'. (3) R22-RC-A: 'private prior stays unknown to slightly negative because the refiner was trained on train embryos'. The 09:35Z read kept 'the card's CI caveat applies'. WHAT CHANGED: (a) Probe 48 IS the like-for-like record that was missing: the same file minus CI is exp70g at 0.956, and exp79a reads 0.957 with 33 TeamIds passed, which is a real crossing, not a tie. The public embryo is neither of the two train embryos (discussion 743006: embryo = id prefix, train = 44b6 71 + 6bba 128 movies), so this is an out-of-embryo transfer read for the refiner, the exact test the 'in-sample' caveat asked for. (b) Mechanism, measured today: CI lowers the matched localisation error on 4/4 lab clips in BOTH embryos (44b6 -0.054/-0.082 um; 6bba -0.284/-0.155 um). It does this without any fitted offset: z bias is unchanged, and the gain comes from averaging two estimators whose errors are ~0.45 um apart. That is a variance cut, which is not an embryo-specific convention, unlike Canh's constant shift or the head199 retrain that failed across embryos. (c) The downside is bounded: topology is byte-identical, and CI coverage is fail-soft (videos not refined keep K2 rows). NEW VERDICT: the 'public-only / unknown-to-negative' part is OVERTURNED. Private prior for CI vs the same file without CI: P(>= 0) ~0.65-0.75, central ~+0.0005 on private (single-embryo public evidence, refiner in-sample lab). The remaining real caveats are only two. (1) The public read is one embryo. (2) CI files have L ~9.3-9.5 h, so a CI final must be submitted by ~09:30Z 29 Sep. This supports the 10:16Z private-hedge proposal (exp75 = #37 + CI) and a finals pair with a CI file on the public side.
